title: NYAM sweep and failed breakout
source: Raw September 8 explicitly waits for the completed 09–10 range, then a low sweep, failure/reclaim and a long toward its high; August 28 shows the high-side short mirror. September 8 range H 29686.75 comes from the 09:30 wick, not the earlier candle body, while range L is about 29455 and PDL about 29469 is a separate reclaim. However, its drawn stop 29436.75 lies ABOVE the full sweep low near 29424. FORMULAS’ universal sweep-wick stop is therefore not established by that drawing; its separate “49.75 above PDL” description is an entry-to-stop distance misread. Original stop revisions remain unavailable. The August 31 pre-10 short is another model, not permission to use an unfinished 09–10 box.
finding: The source-dated August 28 replay places the NQ 09–10 box at H 29703.25 / L 29562.75, consistent in position and path with the approximate MNQ source bounds near 29704 / 29562. The code nevertheless accepts any beyond-edge wick, groups five observed rows, timestamps confirmation at block start and retains no stop/target episode or freshness ledger. Extended high/low lines persist after their visits. Source snapshot targets, pending limits and realized fills are not interchangeable.
fix: Preserve the source contradiction explicitly: do not rewrite FORMULAS or implement an assumed universal stop beyond the full sweep wick. Store separately any original stop order, subsequent stop revision, position-tool drawing and actual sweep extreme. Mark missing initial risk as unknown.

Construct H=max(high), L=min(low) over the complete declared 09:00–10:00 interval and freeze at 10:00. Record instrument, contract, timezone, actual contributing bars and coverage. Compare NQ versus MNQ only with their feed/basis difference stated; do not force approximate screenshot labels onto exact NQ ticks.

Apply the user’s September 11 clarification to BOTH highs and lows independently: freeze each reference under its own ID; scan all prices from known_at; store first_revisit_at; end the active line at that first visit. An exact visit consumes freshness even if it is shallower than the named two-tick sweep threshold. The episode begun on that visit can still confirm afterward, but later revisits cannot be new fresh setups. A new completed hour/session creates a new reference; missing intervening coverage makes freshness unknown. Keep historical box geometry separate from active target lines.

Unify the two failure detectors into an event routine with explicit depth, clock-bar size and expiry. For the existing named research variant: high sweep >=H+2 ticks or low sweep <=L−2 ticks; confirmation is a complete five-minute close strictly inside (L,H), known at its actual end, within 30 minutes of the sweep. Keep the author’s unspecified numerical thresholds separate from those defaults.

Return one episode with reference ID, side, first visit, sweep time/extreme, first inside close and expiry/invalidation. Include the sweep-containing five-minute bar when its close follows the sweep; inspect execution order or mark ambiguity if needed. A later failed attempt cannot reset the original reference’s freshness.

Attach opposite-edge reach, PDL/PDH confluence and optional TDO close as separate ordered outcomes. Freeze the selected target before the trade and verify it was still unvisited then. Report day-level any-failure, failure given eligible first sweeps, and target reach given confirmation under precise separate labels. Never count parked limits or drawn potential R as fills.
acceptance: July 10, 2026: H 29968.50 / L 29790.50; first low revisit/sweep is 10:32, inside close 29881.25 is known 10:40, and the previously unvisited high is first reached 11:25. The low line ends at 10:32 and high line at 11:25; the 11:00-area repeat low visit is not fresh.
October 8, 2025: first high visit/sweep at 10:00 receives no five-minute inside close by 10:30. A later return must not rearm that high or pass the original 30-minute variant.

August 28, 2026: replay H 29703.25 / L 29562.75, high sweep at 10:00 and inside close known 10:05 reproduce the source order. The source 10:13 snapshot has reached the first opposite-edge objective but not the lower remaining limits or final drawing target.

A one-tick visit retires freshness but fails the two-tick sweep variant. A confirming bar starting 29 minutes after the sweep and ending 34 minutes after fails expiry. Removing one minute must make that clock bar incomplete rather than shift its alignment.
September 8 drawing entry 29469.25, stop 29436.75 and target 29686.75 must remain separate from the lower full sweep wick, the range-low reclaim, the PDL reclaim and four uneven pending exits.
fixture: helper checks pass; producer uses a different depth / grouping engine
definition_decision: The initial stop placement and modification history cannot be recovered from a final position-tool drawing. Do not promote it to a universal mechanical stop rule.

title: 09:30 manipulation and reclaim
source: Raw September 1 reply 2094833602018038153 explicitly states the 09:30 manipulation below, reclaim, long toward a retracement and stop at lows. The older pack quotes it. It does not publish a complete hold duration, impulse-selection rule or expiry. Raw five-minute confirmation wording is explicit for PDL/TDO episodes; it does not independently make every 09:30 reclaim identical. April 28 and August 31 screenshots demonstrate other pre-10 trades but do not disclose this full long recipe. Source hold/target semantics remain incomplete.
finding: The current implementation scans the AM window for a two-tick undercut then a five-minute reclaim, with equality accepted and no hold or target episode. Exact July 10 bars show its FIRST undercut is already in the 09:30 bar, and the first sampled reclaim close 29902.75 is known 09:35, not the later 09:45 reclaim described in the earlier audit. A later large undercut proves the bare flag does not certify sustained hold.
fix: Keep the qualitative source recipe incomplete until its hold and impulse-selection rules are documented. Do not turn the pack’s wording into an invented universal hold duration, 09:45 deadline or automatic long/short mirror.

Use the actual 09:30 opening print with known_at=09:30; missing opening data makes the level unavailable. Evaluate subsequent prices including the opening bar only with causal ordering. Preserve opening-price lifecycle separately from the user’s first-visit retirement rule for session highs/lows; any high/low used as a confluence or target must satisfy that rule on both sides.

For the explicitly named two-tick/five-minute variant, require low<=open−2 ticks and a complete close STRICTLY above open, timestamped at the five-minute end. Keep event timestamps, side, sweep extreme and expiry; use a corresponding separately named upper-side variant only if selected, not an unmarked source equivalence.

Expose the unspecified hold rule as a required definition or a clearly named research parameter set: duration, allowed closes, tolerance and invalidation. Record the initial sweep low as an observation; do not assume every final chart stop equals it.

If adding retracement outcomes later, freeze the preceding completed impulse and 50–61.8 pocket before entry, or leave that outcome unavailable. Check target freshness for any referenced high/low. Report reclaim, declared hold and target reach separately, with outcome order and censoring.
acceptance: July 10, 2026: first qualifying undercut is 09:30; the 09:30–09:35 group ends at 09:35 with close 29902.75. Store that completion time, not 09:34 and not the later 09:45 reclaim.
January 10, 2025: 09:30 open 21192.50 is undercut and no completed AM reclaim above it occurs. Pre-open bars do not confirm a level before its opening print.
A close exactly equal to the open fails strict reclaim. A later breach invalidates a declared hold variant but does not erase the historical fact that an earlier reclaim occurred.
Appending AM extrema cannot change a target impulse already selected; absent source hold parameters remain unknown, not automatic success.
definition_decision: Need a source definition of hold and preceding impulse for this specific 09:30 model; the raw pre-10 screenshots do not supply those numerical rules.

title: TDO close-through after a named sweep
source: Raw September 9 replies explicitly correct the level to the MIDNIGHT opening price. September 3 names a close below it after an Asia-high sweep “in this case,” and September 9 shows a completed-range high sweep followed by a separate TDO crossing. A later literal TDO retest is not universal: the actual September 9 retracement peaks below TDO despite an illustrative zigzag touching it. A TDO wick alone is not the named-edge sweep, and a Pine touch statistic is another event.
finding: The producer treats the first AM bar already beyond TDO as a wick, chooses its earliest side, and looks for an opposite close without any separate reference ID. It can miss a later genuine crossing and has no overnight association. January 28’s undercut/reclaim around 09:36–09:39 remains a retained false because the earlier already-above-TDO state selected the opposite branch. The source’s high/low reference must also have been fresh before its first sweep.
fix: Create TDO from the actual declared-midnight opening print, retaining contract, price, timestamp, clock evidence and coverage. Do not take a later minute if midnight is absent or infer a screenshot TDO tick from its adjacent entry label.

Consume a named reference-sweep episode with reference_id, high/low side, known_at, first_visit and sweep_time. Apply the user’s freshness requirement to BOTH swept highs and lows from their own completion time, including visits before the AM scan. A previously consumed reference cannot be a fresh setup.

For a high-side sweep, search subsequent complete five-minute closes below TDO; for a low-side sweep, search above TDO. Preserve the actual close-completion time and specified expiry/invalidation. A close may confirm the same first-visit episode after its reference line has stopped.

Maintain standalone TDO touch, actual cross and sweep-linked confirmation as separate events. Starting a window wholly above or below TDO is a state, not a newly observed sweep. Scan causally linked episodes rather than choosing a single first side for the whole day.

Support the explicitly scoped overnight and AM variants with separate eligible sweep populations. Do not make TDO confirmation mandatory in source rows where it is optional, impose an exact TDO retest from a blue schematic, or transfer Pine’s 08–16 touch denominator to this setup.
acceptance: A path starting below TDO with no separate named-edge sweep has no source TDO-confirmation setup, even if it later closes above TDO.

January 28, 2026: TDO 26220.25 is undercut around 09:36–09:38 and reclaimed; preserve this real crossing while requiring a separately identified fresh reference sweep before it can qualify as the source setup.
An Asia-high first sweep at 01:10 followed by a completed 01:30 close below TDO belongs to that overnight episode. An AM-only flag cannot supply or erase its confirmation.
September 9 midnight correction remains authoritative. A source retracement that peaks below TDO must not fail an invented exact-retest requirement; the projected blue zigzag is not an execution.
Consuming one reference high does not consume the opposite low or a newly completed hour’s high. Missing intervening bars makes freshness unknown, not fresh.
leakage: confirmation timing / unlinked sweep / consumed-reference reuse
definition_decision: The midnight definition is resolved by raw author replies; preserve date-specific clock evidence and leave any exact crowded source TDO tick unclaimed.

title: Unfilled NWOG as a destination
source: Raw August 17 explicitly describes a New York-open short after a midnight sweep/failure and closes when NWOG is hit. August 3 names a fresh gap printed Sunday at 6PM EST. finding: Current code uses Friday 15:59 one-minute close and Sunday 18:00 open, whereas FORMULAS’ preferred endpoint is Friday 16:59 close. It scores only Monday AM aggregate overlap and ignores prior visits, live state, entry direction and target chronology. August 31’s plotted band was already traded overnight before the AM re-touch; August 24’s band was also visited Sunday but is not reached during AM. Neither is a fresh unfilled-gap AM target.
fix: Keep Friday 15:59-close and 16:59-close as explicitly named endpoint variants pending a source definition; do not relabel either as settlement. Use the instrument exchange calendar and actual completed last-trading-session print around holidays. Preserve the underlying contract and endpoint timestamps.

Define gap formation separately from a later visit: the Sunday opening endpoint creates the interval and cannot, by itself, make every gap instantly retired. Store lower/upper boundaries, formation_time and the published or explicitly named post-formation return rule. Leave faithful semantics unresolved if the source does not settle them.

Maintain an ordered gap state: formed, active, first tagged, retired. Scan the entire post-formation history, not only 09:30 onward. At a candidate entry require a still-live destination ahead of the trade; approach determines the near edge. Keep exact edge touch, named two-tick proximity and full-gap traversal as separate observations.

Link the entry’s midnight/open/high-low failure episode by ID, then measure first subsequent near-edge tag by the declared noon/RTH-close horizons. Apply the user’s first-revisit rule to any session-high/low trigger independently of the gap’s own formation convention.

Preserve the old any-AM-overlap field only as a descriptive comparison. Report eligible active gaps, confirmed entries with a live destination, post-entry first tags and censored/invalidated outcomes separately. A scheduled limit or source arrow is not an observed fill.

August 24, 2026 code band [29392.25,29395.75] is visited Sunday, while AM remains below it. Distinguish already-retired from still-active-but-not-hit and from a plain AM negative.
A formation opening print must not create and retire every gap simultaneously. Test a gap above and below price with the appropriate near edge and actual post-formation chronology.
An unavailable Friday endpoint or missing intervening trading produces unknown eligibility. A pre-entry tag never counts as the entry’s destination outcome.
September 8 source NWOG 29530.50/29524.75 must not be replaced by AS.L 29571.00 or treated as reached while current price remains above them.

title: Golden-pocket continuation

FORMULAS allows that box as if interchangeable with the measured source impulse. The scorer then uses only gp_touch, while its separate rejection helper is not the stated source sequence. Consume repaired G01/G02/G03 event records, with all individually eligible completed hours. Keep sweep-only, confirmed-failure, author grade and a clearly named mechanical research grade distinct. A day-level OR may be retained only as has_qualifying_setup.

Replace pass=True grading fixtures with actual event assertions and correct the report’s sweep-only description. Test wrong-reference, wrong-side, after-entry, consumed-reference and missing-coverage cases explicitly.

Only report outcomes conditional on concrete event grades and valid post-entry horizons. Multiple copied accounts or partial fills cannot become independent A+ signals; unknown original risk or fill history remains unknown.

August 25, 2026 Asia high 29190 breaks/holds and NYAM low 29279.25 breaks after 10:00 without timely failure; the retained three-box label is false. Do not infer a universal author B+ grade from that limited scan.
An Asia sweep and NYAM failure cannot be combined into a single setup; same-key pairing remains required. A consumed level cannot become fresh after a reset or later visit.
September 10’s explicit no-A+ commentary must not be overridden by inferring a range-low failure from glyphs actually above that low or from the forming 10–11 box.
